<description>
Kernel logging is inherently global: `KernelLogger` is a process-wide
singleton, so every connection receives every log entry and shares the
minimum level. Multiple `btck_LoggingConnection` handles give the false
impression of independent loggers.

Limit `btck_global_logging_connection_create` to a single connection, so
that the globalness is expressed in that one function and the rest of
the interface can operate on the connection handle.

A single connection also makes it straightforward to invoke the callback
without holding the logger's mutex. Holding it serializes all logging
threads on user code, and deadlocks if anything on the callback's thread
logs, e.g. a garbage collector running finalizers that destroy kernel
objects.

Behaviour changes for consumers:
- `btck_logging_connection_create` is renamed to
  `btck_global_logging_connection_create`, and fails if a connection
  already exists.
- `btck_logging_set_min_level` becomes
  `btck_logging_connection_set_min_level`, and each new connection
  starts at `Info`.
- The "Logger connected." `Debug` entry is removed, since it can no
  longer be delivered.
- The callback can be invoked from multiple threads at the same time,
  so it must be thread-safe. Destroying the connection still waits for
  running invocations to return.
</description>

[2026-11-04] rc:4473236493 inline on src/kernel/bitcoinkernel.h by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-05):
In commit "kernel: invoke the logging callback without holding the lock" (f4e0a6faf76dafe13b474a006fac57dfb4ebec75)

Reviewing this commit I found a few things, which #36768 handles, in case they're useful:

- A callback that destroys its own connection now hangs, because destroy waits for running invocations, including the one it's called from. At Debug level the "Logger disconnecting." entry reaches the callback first, so it recurses. I checked both with a scratch test. In [#36768](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36768), destroying a connection doesn't wait for a running call, so a callback can destroy any connection, including its own.
- With the lock gone, "must not call any other kernel API function" is stricter than needed, and the GC case depends on more being allowed (a finalizer destroying kernel objects, which logs). [#36768](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36768) documents what's safe, that entries from different threads have no order, and that a callback shouldn't wait on threads that may hold internal locks like `cs_main`.
- Nothing tests logging from inside a callback, the deadlock this fixes. [#36768](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36768) adds that test, which hangs before the fix.

If you'd rather keep the fix in this PR, we can bring these changes over, but would like try to unbundle separate issues.

_Edit: now points to #36768, which replaces #36766._
[2026-11-04] r:5775672229 review COMMENTED by ryanofsky (member) (edited 2026-11-05):
Code review f4e0a6faf76dafe13b474a006fac57dfb4ebec75

Concept ACK on calling the callback without holding the lock. I reviewed all the code here, and since the deadlock fix doesn't depend on the rest of the PR, I opened #36768 with just that fix for the current multi-connection logger, with no API change. The fix doesn't depend on having a single connection, so I'm hoping it can go in separately and this PR can rebase on it. That would let us make progress where we agree while we work out the rest.

Thanks for reworking the API. The first version replaced `btck_LoggingConnection` with a single global callback, so keeping the connection handle with a level setter that takes it is a real improvement: callers hold a connection and pass it where it's needed, they can't interfere with each other's callbacks, and they track what they own.

Where I'm still stuck is not requiring clients to attach a connection to what it should receive entries from. I think we've been talking past each other, so let me put my side as a concrete outcome. If a client is written assuming one global connection receives every entry, and we later add per-context logging and narrow what the global connection receives, that client has to be restructured to get a connection to every place it creates a context, possibly across package and language boundaries for bindings. If clients attach connections from the start, the same client code keeps working when better logging features arrive, and we don't need errors like "A logging connection already exists".

I understand the reasons given so far as "logging is inherently global" and avoiding a false impression of independent loggers, but I haven't been able to turn them into a concrete outcome like that. Is there a case where requiring clients to attach connections leads to a problem for a client, or for us? If you can describe one, I think that's what would let us find an API that satisfies both. This PR and #33847 have been getting closer to each other, so I'm hopeful we can get there.

_Edit: now points to #36768, which replaces #36766 and fixes the same deadlock using btcsignals. #36766 has a comparison of the two._
